The Court made the following:
 THE HONOURABLE DR JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA  WRIT PETITION NO: 15082/2024 ORDER:
-
This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India with the following prayer for:
"...to issue an appropriate Writ, Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of MANDAMUS declaring the action of the Respondents in interfere with the life and limb of the petitioners without there being any case registered against them as arbitrary, illegal and violative of fundamental rights guaranteed under Article. 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents not to interfere with the petitioners life and limb in any manner and pass..."
2. Heard Sri Sai Gangadhar Chamarty, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri P.Ajay Babu,
learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that it is a case of interference of police in the civil disputes.

sentences.text: 4. Sri P.Ajay Babu, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, on written instructions, would submit that based on the complaint lodged by Sri Pilli Jatlayya, respondent-police was registered a case against the petitioners in Cr.No.40 of 2024 U/Section 420, 506 r/w 34 of IPC dated 29.03.2024.
He would further submit that, the petitioners were called to the police station relating to the investigation of the said cases.
Except registration of the said crime, respondent police never interfered in the life and limb of the petitioners.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that, recording the same, the writ petition may be disposed of.
6. Recording the above said submissions, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
However, police are directed not to interfere in the civil disputes except under due process of law.
There shall be no order as to costs.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
